external_entities.name: customer company
external_entities.description: A customer business using the invoicing service as a tenant.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

external_entities.name: customer user
external_entities.description: A person at a customer company who uses the billing app as an admin or viewer.
external_entities.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
external_entities.notes: Users are either admins or viewers. They sign in with an email address and a password and get a session cookie. There is no second factor.

external_entities.name: payer
external_entities.description: The person who receives an invoice email and views the payment page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each invoice email sends the payer a link

external_entities.name: support agent
external_entities.description: A support employee who uses the admin console to open billing-app sessions as customer users.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.
external_entities.notes: Each agent signs in with their own account and a one-time code.

processes.name: billing app
processes.description: The shared application used by customer users, which accesses tenant data, queues PDF render jobs, and fetches PDFs.
processes.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app
processes.notes: The app adds the company filter to each query itself. Nobody wrote down whether it checks that an invoice belongs to the user's company, or whether it checks the user's role again when a request arrives. It trusts the company ID carried by PDF render jobs and uses one service credential for all companies when fetching PDFs.

processes.name: PDF renderer
processes.description: A renderer that consumes render jobs, reads invoices, and writes PDFs to the shared PDF bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
processes.notes: It trusts the company ID the job carries. Nobody recorded how the renderer reaches the database, the queue or the bucket.

processes.name: admin console
processes.description: A console reachable from the support office network that lets an agent open a billing-app session as any customer user.
processes.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
processes.notes: The console is reachable only from the support office network. Its hosting location was not stated.

data_stores.name: tenant database
data_stores.description: The shared PostgreSQL database containing every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The billing app keeps every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details in one PostgreSQL database, the tenant database.
data_stores.notes: Every table has a company ID column. The database has no row-level security, and the app connects with one database account for all companies. Nobody recorded how the database is protected at rest.

data_stores.name: render queue
data_stores.description: The queue holding PDF render jobs containing a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue
data_stores.notes: Nobody recorded how the billing app and the renderer reach the queue.

data_stores.name: PDF bucket
data_stores.description: The shared bucket where rendered PDFs are stored under a company ID and invoice number.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_stores.notes: Nobody recorded how the bucket is protected at rest.

data_flows.name: use billing app
data_flows.description: A customer user uses the billing app to view and edit invoice data.
data_flows.source_excerpt: People at a customer company use the billing app in their browser over HTTPS.
data_flows.notes: The invoice edit form posts the whole invoice back, and the billing app saves every field it receives, including the paid flag and the company's payout bank account.
data_flows.authentication: email address and password; session cookie; second factor none
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customer information, payout bank details, credentials and session information

data_flows.name: view payment page
data_flows.description: A payer follows an invoice link and views the invoice, company name and bank details on the payment page.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The payment page shows the invoice, the company's name and its bank details
data_flows.data_description: Invoice, company name and company bank details

data_flows.name: read and save data
data_flows.description: The billing app reads and writes tenant records in the shared database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app adds the company filter to each query itself
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the billing app reaches the database.
data_flows.authentication: one database account shared by all companies
data_flows.data_description: Invoices, customers and payout bank details

data_flows.name: enqueue render job
data_flows.description: The billing app places a PDF render job on the render queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the billing app puts a render job on the render queue
data_flows.notes: The job carries a company ID and an invoice number. Nobody recorded how the billing app reaches the queue.

data_flows.name: read render job
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer takes render jobs from the queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The PDF renderer takes jobs off the queue one at a time
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the renderer reaches the queue.

data_flows.name: read invoice
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer reads an invoice from the tenant database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: reads the invoice from the tenant database
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the renderer reaches the database.

data_flows.name: write PDF
data_flows.description: The PDF renderer writes a rendered PDF to the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the PDF to the PDF bucket under the company ID and the invoice number
data_flows.notes: Nobody recorded how the renderer reaches the bucket.
data_flows.data_description: Rendered PDF, company ID and invoice number

data_flows.name: fetch PDF
data_flows.description: The billing app fetches PDFs from the PDF bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The billing app fetches PDFs from the bucket with one service credential for all companies.
data_flows.authentication: one service credential shared for all companies

data_flows.name: sign in console
data_flows.description: A support agent signs in to the admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: each agent signs in to it with their own account and a one-time code
data_flows.notes: The admin console is reachable only from the support office network.

data_flows.name: open user session
data_flows.description: The admin console opens a billing-app session as any customer user.
data_flows.source_excerpt: From the admin console an agent can open a session in the billing app as any customer user.
data_flows.notes: Everything the agent then does is recorded against the customer user, not against the agent.

trust_boundaries.name: customer company
trust_boundaries.description: The tenant boundary for a customer company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Each customer company is one tenant

trust_boundaries.name: cloud platform
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud platform containing the shared billing app, tenant database and PDF bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: all companies share one billing app, one database and one PDF bucket in our cloud platform

trust_boundaries.name: support office network
trust_boundaries.description: The network from which support agents work and the admin console is reachable.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our support agents work from the support office network.

assumptions.assumption: The tenant database is confidential because it contains invoices, customer information and payout bank details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains every company's invoices, customers and payout bank details.

assumptions.assumption: The PDF bucket is confidential because it stores rendered PDFs of invoices and related company information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the renderer writes PDFs to the bucket under the company ID and invoice number, and the PDFs are generated from invoices.
